key_insight: Token-level rewards can be extracted from an existing process reward model without extra training by attributing the final reward to each token via a single gradient-based pass.
engineering_relevance: This enables much finer credit assignment for RL training of language models, improving optimization efficiency while avoiding the cost of building a separate token reward model.
method: Define each token’s influence as the change in final reward when it is replaced by a semantically null token.
Approximate this influence with a first-order Taylor expansion using the token-embedding difference and the reward gradient.
Compute token-level rewards with one forward and one backward pass instead of N forward passes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong benchmark gains, including +4.9% on MathVista for Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct and +11.5% on AIME24 for Qwen2.5-Math-7B.
watch_item: The approximation depends on the quality of the null-token substitution and the local linearity assumption, so attribution accuracy may degrade for highly nonlinear cases.
paper_title: Unlocking Token Rewards via Training-Free Reward Attribution
